paragraphs: Here's what Moses is getting at, friend. Everybody in Israel is under something bigger than their own opinion. Judges in every town, a verdict at the place the LORD will choose, and a king who answers to the same instruction as everyone else (Deut 16:18; 17:8-11, 18-19). Nobody gets to run on their own say-so, not the little guy and not the guy with the crown.

Now look at what keeps all of it honest. Moses says a bribe "blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous" (Deut 16:19). Even good, smart people can get bent when something shiny shows up. That's why the king has to write out his own copy of the instruction and read it "all the days of his life" (Deut 17:19). I'm telling you, that's not a one-time read, that's a daily check-up. Horses, wives, silver and gold all pull on the heart, and the scroll pulls it back (Deut 17:16-17).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Your heart needs the Word more than once. Open it, let it correct you, and keep coming back, because staying close to what God said is how you keep from drifting to the right or the left (Deut 17:20). The king who did that wouldn't be lifted up above his countrymen, and that's a good lesson for the rest of us too. Moses isn't done preaching yet, and I'm not done baking, so stay with me.
